name: Janismo
summary: Janismo is the personalist, moralising political style of Jânio Quadros: a leader above parties who promises to sweep corruption out of government with a broom. Its stated programme joined austerity and anti-inflation policy at home with an independent foreign policy, ties to socialist and newly independent states and opposition to colonialism and intervention.
scope: The movement around Jânio Quadros (1947-1961), as scholars of the janista discourse describe it (FAPESP, Queler, FGV Atlas): moralism, anti-party personalism and the 1960 broom campaign, with the programme he stated and enacted as president. It excludes the UDN's wider programme and later politicians called janist.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Quadros's inaugural address and resignation letter denounce corruption, favouritism and scandal in the established political system, and the FAPESP scholarship calls moralism the fundamental appeal of the janista discourse.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Razões da Renúncia says the people overflowed the parties and condemned their methods; scholarship on the janista discourse describes parties and Congress as disturbers of order and a strong leader as sufficient.

strong-leader.rationale: The janista programme rested on one leader with power to decide and extirpate corruption, and Quadros tried to centralise decisions in the Presidency at Congress's expense.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The inaugural address condemns budget deficits and paper-money issue, and his government pursued a conservative anti-inflation policy and exchange reform.

price-stability-first.rationale: His domestic policy is described as conservative and centred on fighting inflation, and the inaugural address blames inflation for the cost of living crisis.

non-intervention.rationale: The 1961 message to Congress asks that each Latin American country keep its self-determination free of outside intervention and of its own intervention in others' affairs; the resignation text restates self-determination and non-intervention.

national-self-determination.rationale: The message to Congress lists the self-determination of peoples among its aims and backs independence for all colonial peoples.

independent-unions.rationale: The FGV Atlas names defence of union freedom against the state as one of the janista proposals, and the inaugural address says freedom of union organisation and the right to strike belong to the concept of the regime.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: His government issued small decrees aimed at moral sanitation, and scholarship describes his moralism as joining public and private spheres and exalting conservative morals.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The message to Congress rejects every form of colonialism and imperialism.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He wants all colonial peoples independent as soon as possible, which excludes rule by an advanced society.

one-party-rule.rationale: The inaugural address presents democracy as a clash of interests, and criticises one-patron systems where all reclamation is forbidden; his own movement stayed outside party machinery.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He rejects Soviet-style systems, in which the inaugural address says liberties are abolished and criticism suppressed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The inaugural address criticises regimes that abolish liberty and suppress criticism and urges conserving freedoms.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The inaugural address criticises states that replace distribution of land with its nationalisation.

class-collaboration.rationale: The inaugural address calls for solidarity and co-responsibility of capital, workers, civilians and military, and says workers pursue their interests within the democratic system and with discipline.

state-harmful.rationale: He describes the state as 'all of us', builder and supervisor of collective wealth, which contradicts calling it unnecessary and harmful.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The inaugural address says democracy strengthens itself through state action in the field of private initiative: guiding, undertaking and complementing it.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He declared Brazil's ideological position Western and unchanging, yet sought relations with socialist states and an independent line; the sources point both ways.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The message to Congress says Brazil stays faithful to the inter-American system and keeps its Western commitments.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The message to Congress calls strengthening the United Nations essential, while calling it less than a super-state.

defeat-communism.rationale: He fought domestic communists yet pursued peaceful coexistence and relations with socialist states.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: His resignation text says his true nationalism repels both the sovietisation of the country and the dictatorship of economic power.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The message to Congress calls eliminating the north-south gap the most important aim of the Western world, and he sought long-term European financing for development.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He asks Europe to update import tariffs and credit terms in light of Brazil's industrialisation and speaks of defending basic commodities.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: His government renegotiated and committed to repay the foreign debt, and the inaugural address says it must be honoured dollar by dollar.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: His record is of seeking foreign loans and refinancing, and he calls Brazil avid for capital.

ban-cartels.rationale: He sent Congress an anti-trust bill, which he says was mutilated.

no-business-privileges.rationale: He denounces favouritism and says his government would discipline economic power while respecting private enterprise.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: His non-intervention principle excludes sending troops into another state.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: His non-intervention principle excludes arming insurgents against other governments.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He describes Brazil as free of prejudice of race, colour or creed.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He calls Brazil a people in which colour, religion and party are irrelevant and the individual counts for what he is.

religious-nation.rationale: The same passage makes religion irrelevant to belonging to the Brazilian people.
